Indus Capital Advisory is preparing an educational guide for corporate treasury managers contrasting the operational mechanics of the Money Market and the Capital Market. The report highlights that the Money Market deals exclusively in short-term debt instruments with maturities up to one year, serving liquidity adjustments for commercial banks, the central government, and major corporations. Because money market instruments like Treasury Bills, Call Money, and Certificates of Deposit involve high unit denominations (often Rs. 25,00,000 or multiples of Rs. 25,000 for T-Bills), the participants are predominantly institutional bodies.
